card: This pull request optimizes descriptor parsing, particularly for descriptors containing extended public and private keys. Previously, the parser invoked both extended private and public key decoding for every key, redundantly running Base58Check and double-SHA256 passes twice per key, while descriptor checksumming relied on linear string searches. This PR combines the decoding steps into a single Base58Check pass, replaces checksum charset lookups with an O(1) table, and updates string passing to string_view. The author reports a 29.4% speedup parsing a large multisig descriptor in microbenchmarks, motivated by slow wallet fuzz targets.
evidence: Author microbenchmark on a 20-of-20 Taproot multisig descriptor showed ParseDescriptor execution time dropping from 127,812 ns to 90,253 ns (~29.4% speedup) (PR description).
Author identified the bottleneck while running wallet fuzz targets that spent excessive time in descriptor parsing (PR description).
problem: When parsing extended keys in descriptors, the parser unconditionally attempted both private and public extended key decoding, executing two separate Base58Check decodings and double-SHA256 checksums per key when only one could succeed. Additionally, checksum calculations used linear scans across character sets, and key decoding APIs forced heap allocations via temporary strings, noticeably slowing down descriptor parsing and wallet fuzz targets.
scope_notes: Updates key decoding and Base58 decoding signatures across src/base58.h and src/key_io.h to accept std::string_view.
summary: Optimizes descriptor parsing performance for descriptors containing extended keys (xpub and xprv). It merges separate extended private and public key decoding routines into a single Base58Check decoding step, avoiding duplicate cryptographic hashing. It also replaces linear charset searches in descriptor checksum computation with a precomputed 256-byte lookup table and updates Base58 decoding APIs to accept std::string_view.
